extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Health Insurance Exchange officials, issuers, policy stakeholders, and public commenters on ACA eligibility verification rules
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory changes and interpretive guidance for verifying household income, resolving income data matching inconsistencies (DMIs), and modifying annual redetermination/automatic re-enrollment procedures for APTC and CSRs under the ACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for creating an annual income data matching (DMI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange would follow the procedures in §155.315(f)(1) through (4) to create an annual income data matching DMI for consumers if: (1) The consumer attested to projected annual household income between 100 percent and 400 percent of the FPL; (2) the Exchange has data from IRS and SSA that indicates household income is below 100 percent of the FPL; (3) the Exchange has not assessed or determined the consumer to have income within the Medicaid or CHIP eligibility standard; and (4) the consumer's attested projected annual household income exceeds the income reflected in the data available from electronic data sources by a reasonable threshold established by the Exchange and approved by HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We propose that a reasonable threshold must not be less than 10 percent and can also include a threshold dollar amount. The Exchange would use the §155.315(f)(1)-(4) procedures to resolve the DMI; if an applicant fails to provide documentation, the Exchange would redetermine eligibility based on available IRS data, which typically results in discontinuing APTC and CSR as required in §155.320(c)(3)(vi)(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration and comment solicitation for the 'reasonable threshold' for DMIs
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed 'reasonable threshold' used to determine when an attested projected income exceeds the income reflected in trusted electronic data must not be less than 10 percent and may include a dollar-amount component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS welcomes comments and data to help ensure the threshold is properly calibrated to maximize program integrity while minimizing unnecessary administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative burden estimates and timelines for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS estimates that answering verification questions and submitting supporting documents would take consumers approximately 1 hour, and that 90 days is provided to resolve a DMI (with the ability to request an extension in certain circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS believes the 1-hour burden is minimal and outweighed by APTC benefits and by reducing improper enrollment; welcomes comments on accuracy of the administrative burden estimate and on whether consumers can reasonably obtain documentation within the 90-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when tax return data is unavailable (removal of §155.320(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.320(c)(5), which currently requires Exchanges to accept self-attestation when IRS confirms no tax return data is available, and instead require Exchanges to verify household income with other trusted data sources and follow the full alternative verification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change would eliminate the exception that allowed attestation without further verification when IRS data were unavailable; HHS concludes that the statutory framework requires following the full verification/alternative verification process when tax data are unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory two-step process for addressing income inconsistencies (section 1411(e)(4)(A) of the ACA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges must (1) make a reasonable effort to identify and address causes of income inconsistencies (including contacting the applicant to confirm accuracy and other actions the Secretary may identify) and (2) if step one does not resolve the inconsistency, notify the applicant and provide an opportunity to present documentary evidence or resolve the inconsistency with the source of the DMI during the 90-day period after the notice is sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS implemented these requirements at §155.315(f)(1) through (4); there is no statutory exception to this process and §155.320(c)(5) conflicted with this statutory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on HHS flexibility to modify verification procedures (interpretation of §§1411(c)(4)(B) and 1412(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory flexibility in §1411(c)(4)(B) to 'modify the methods used under the program established by this section for the Exchange and verification of information' applies primarily to how information is exchanged and verified between HHS and trusted data sources, and the term 'modify' connotes moderate change — not wholesale suspension of verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1412(b)(2) does not provide a blanket permissive exception to the verification framework; HHS's reading is that these statutory provisions do not authorize creating exceptions that bypass the basic verification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual redetermination rule for 'fully subsidized' enrollees (require active confirmation or $5 monthly premium)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.335(a)(3) and (n): when an enrollee does not submit an application for an updated eligibility determination by the last day to select a plan for January 1 coverage, and the enrollee's portion of the premium for the entire policy would be $0 after application of APTC (a 'fully subsidized enrollee'), Exchanges must decrease the amount of the APTC applied so the remaining monthly premium owed by the enrollee for the entire policy equals $5 for the first month and every following month the enrollee does not confirm or update eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollees automatically re-enrolled with a $5 monthly premium may submit an application at any point to confirm eligibility and reinstate the full amount of APTC prospectively. Proposed implementation: FFEs and SBE-FPs must implement starting with benefit year 2026 redeterminations; State Exchanges starting with benefit year 2027. HHS seeks comment on whether $5 is appropriate, alternative dollar amounts, whether APTC payments should be made for automatically re-enrolled fully subsidized individuals, and whether program integrity concerns outweigh benefits of automatic re-enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that fully subsidized enrollees affirmatively confirm eligibility to continue zero-premium coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: To address improper enrollments and the risk of enrollees being unaware of coverage (often due to agent/broker/web-broker enrollments), HHS proposes requiring qualified enrollees who are redetermined eligible for APTC that fully subsidizes their premium to take an active step to confirm eligibility information before continuing with fully subsidized coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS argues active engagement is necessary because fully subsidized enrollees may not receive premium bills, enabling improper enrollments to continue and risking surprise tax liabilities; HHS seeks comment on outreach alternatives and whether outreach sufficiently prompts action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of eliminating APTC during automatic re-enrollment and assessment of harms
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS considered automatically re-enrolling fully subsidized enrollees without any APTC (which would require them to return to the Exchange to obtain updated eligibility before any APTC is paid), or charging the full premium during automatic re-enrollment, but identified potential harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns include creation of significant debt to issuers, undue financial hardship for enrollees, barriers to accessing coverage, loss of lower-risk enrollees destabilizing the risk pool, and increased uninsured rates. HHS therefore proposes the $5 approach as a balance but seeks comment on alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer handling of past-due premium when imposing a non-zero re-enrollment premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers would be permitted to attribute past-due premium amounts they are owed to the initial premium the enrollee pays to effectuate new coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discussed as an operational consequence to consider if APTC is reduced or eliminated during automatic re-enrollment; HHS notes attributing past-due amounts may create debt and other harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of data/comments regarding program integrity tradeoffs and administrative burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS repeatedly seeks comment on whether proposed verification requirements, thresholds, time burdens, and automatic re-enrollment changes appropriately balance program integrity benefits against administrative burden and consumer harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific requests include data to calibrate thresholds (e.g., the 10% minimum), comments on the 1-hour documentation burden estimate, views on the $5 monthly premium choice and alternative amounts, and whether outreach could be sufficient instead of affirmative action requirements.
